sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: Chips de IA da Nvidia aparecem em data center na China ligado a Alice Huang
sources.text: US$ 5 BILHÕES em chips da NVIDIA desviados para a China?! O caso NVIDIA acaba de ganhar proporções ainda maiores e acendeu um alerta máximo de segurança nacional nos Estados Unidos. Crédito: Pedro Castro Um data center instalado em Xangai, na China, e ligado a empresas associadas a Alice Huang, executiva que está no centro das polêmicas envolvendo a Nvidia, utiliza chips avançados de inteligência artificial da série Blackwell, da gigante dos semicondutores, com restrições de remessa para o país asiático . A informação foi revelada pela Bloomberg nesta sexta-feira (27). Evidências da presença dos componentes, cuja exportação exige licenças especiais do governo dos Estados Unidos, foram encontradas em documentos de empréstimos solicitados pelas empresas Shanghai Shuoyao e Shanghai Kezhan. Eles estariam em uso no complexo de supercomputação Yangtze River Delta Project . Conforme a reportagem, um dos equipamentos é o rack Nvidia GB300 NVL72 , considerado um dos mais potentes da marca. Ele foi oferecido pela Shanghai Shuoyao como garantia para um empréstimo de US$ 14 milhões (R$ 77,5 milhões pela cotação atual) contratado junto ao Banco de Inovação de Xangai. Ele foi listado pela Shanghai Kezhan após a solicitação de um empréstimo equivalente a US$ 13,5 milhões (R$ 74,7 milhões). A operação ocorreu em dezembro do ano passado, por meio de uma empresa de leasing vinculada a uma agência do governo local. Não ficou claro como os equipamentos Nvidia Blackwell chegaram ao país . Como destaca a publicação, geralmente eles passam por várias mãos antes de serem instalados nos data centers, incluindo distribuidores locais, ou são inicialmente vendidos a pessoas em mercados sem restrições e levados para a China por meio de contrabando . Fundada em 2023 por Alice Huang, que teve um caso extraconjugal com o CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang, a Megaspeed possui parceria com a Shuoyao . Ela teria usado uma representação do Yangtze River Delta Project para mostrar aos investidores seu maior data center, conforme a publicação. Além disso, a executiva, investigada por autoridades americanas devido à suspeita de espionagem, possui ligação com várias empresas que investiram no projeto. Uma delas seria a NeXPower Japan, que detém 83,3% da Kezhan . Em meio às polêmicas sobre o caso, a Megaspeed afirmou, recentemente, que Alice deixou a empresa no ano passado. Saiba mais detalhes nesta matéria . sources.name: Engadget
sources.title: Restricted NVIDIA chips were installed at a Chinese data center linked to Alice Huang
sources.text: Bloomberg traced the lineage of one GB300 server rack to Gigabyte Technology. Well, this is awkward. Bloomberg reports it may have found evidence of a link between a Chinese data center with NVIDIA Blackwell hardware and Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang's brief resignation from the company . Looking through documents two different firms submitted to Chinese regulators, the outlet found mention of GB300 NVL72 and GB200 server racks at the Yangtze River Delta Project in Shanghai. One of the companies, Shanghai Shuoyao, listed a GB300 NVL72 rack as collateral to secure an approximately $14 million loan from the Shanghai Innovation Bank. A single GB300 NVL72 unit houses 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Grace processors, and can weigh about 3,300 pounds. US export rules require a license to ship these Blackwell systems to China. As Bloomberg notes, Jensen Huang once claimed GB300 racks are too big to smuggle. It's unclear how the GB300 and GB200 units made their way to the Shanghai facility, which may eventually house as many as 800,000 servers. However, Bloomberg was able to partly track the lineage of the GB300 unit. By putting the serial of the rack into a public warranty database, the outlet was able to trace it back to Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology, which PC gamers will know as one of NVIDIA's many add-in board partners. Like other NVIDIA AIBs, Gigabyte buys GPU chips from the company that it then uses to manufacture graphics cards for consumers and servers for enterprise customers. Gigabyte declined to answer Bloomberg's questions about what company or party originally bought the GB300 rack. A spokesperson told the outlet it "conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations," adding, "all transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time." Shanghai Shuoyao, the company that offered a GB300 as collateral, has ties with Megaspeed. Alice Huang took a controlling stake in the Singaporean cloud computing company in 2023 before leaving it in August 2025. Earlier this month, Shanghai Shuoyao said it was one of Megaspeed's service providers, but described its relationship with the company as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." According to Bloomberg , Megaspeed used renderings of the Yangtze River Delta Project in a presentation it shared with investors in 2024. The deck did not list China as the location of the data center. Bloomberg notes it does not have evidence that Megaspeed directly diverted NVIDIA chips to the data center, and the company denies any wrongdoing . The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules . NVIDIA did not immediately respond to Engadget's comment request. Alice Huang appears to have had a number of other ties to the Yangtze River Delta Project. Most notably, through Kang Wei, the man The New York Times reports was often introduced as her husband and appears to have had ties with China's Ministry of State Security. Bloomberg found him listed as the president of the facility. The publication also found evidence of servers containing NVIDIA's earlier Hopper-generation chips inside the Yangtze River Delta Project. Those GPUs are also illegal to ship to China without permission from the US government. Jensen Huang is set to testify publicly before Congress on December 3 at 10AM ET.

stories.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation

sources.name: Hugging Face
sources.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
sources.text: AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on. Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them. Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation. Sharing how an evaluation was built, including what went wrong, lets others find errors, improve it, and reuse it. The Hugging Face hub is the home for AI evaluation: we host around 3500 eval leaderboards and have seen about a 16X growth in eval datasets on the hub in the past year , to about 17000 datasets. In recent months, we have also incorporated support for agentic abstractions that are relevant to evaluation. For example, Traces that store an agent’s work in an easily reviewable and sharable way; Benchmarks that highlight datasets used to evaluate models with leaderboards; and Environments that show datasets used as agentic RL or evaluation environments. In the research community, AI evaluation terminology is notoriously inconsistent . The glossary at the end defines each term we use and notes the other names you may come across. AI evaluation design has evolved in three forms as language models have become more capable and able to perform more complex work: question answer, agentic, and teams or swarms. Question-answer benchmarks such as MMLU (2020) and GPQA (2023) measure knowledge and reasoning through the answers models produce. As models became capable of planning and using tools, agentic benchmarks such as SWE-bench and WebArena expanded the scope to resolving software issues and completing tasks on websites. These tasks require evaluation setups that account for the environment in which the system operates and the changes it makes. Lately, research on multi-agent systems has started to add another dimension: how agents coordinate and what they accomplish together. This includes decentralized swarms , teams managed by an orchestrator , and specialized agents collaborating on scientific work . Figure 1 shows a rough timeline of these three eras of evaluations. Figure 1. Three types of language model evals. Question-and-answer benchmarks check a response against a key. Agentic benchmarks check what an agent changed in an environment. Team and swarm benchmarks score what a group of agents produced. We’ll focus on agentic evaluations in this article for two reasons. First, they are becoming increasingly the most prominent type in model release announcements due to high user and enterprise interest in agentic deployment. Second, they offer a useful starting point for understanding how evaluation design affects model performance. Team and swarm evaluations introduce further complexity through interactions between agents, which we leave outside the scope of this guide. Once an agent uses tools to complete a task, each part of the surrounding software can affect its score. For instance, in an audit of Terminal-Bench , researchers kept the model fixed and changed the agent harness. Accuracy varied by up to 29.9 percentage points. To understand differences like that, we examine the anatomy of an agentic evaluation and follow one task from the instructions the agent receives to the checks that determine whether it passed. Figure 2. The different components of an agentic evaluation. There are various parts to an agentic evaluation. A task gives the agent its instruction. The agent harness wraps the model and its tools, letting it work inside a pinned environment. During one rollout, the agent attempts the task from start to finish: it may run several commands, inspect their output, and try again before it stops. The evaluation harness runs several rollouts for each task. When a rollout ends, the verifier grades the environment's final state. Each rollout also leaves a trace, and traces and scores together become part of the final published evidence. Each part can be published, inspected, and reused separately. Demand for independent evaluation is growing. Policymakers, enterprises, and researchers want evaluations they can verify, and today they mostly cannot: 98.2% of model-benchmark scores are reported by only one party , and researchers have argued that in-house evaluation is not enough . At the same time, more benchmarks are holding back test items to reduce contamination: questions or solutions entering training data, so scores may reflect prior exposure. Artificial Analysis says 60% of its Intelligence Index v5 , announced in October 2026, rests on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers. Google DeepMind recently piloted double-blind evaluations , where a secure enclave hides an outside evaluator's test prompts from the model provider and the model's weights from the evaluator. While that can reduce contamination, privacy by itself does not guarantee quality, and withholding supporting materials can make expert review harder. We argue that builders can and should still share infrastructure, grading methods, and evidence about task design. Scrutiny depends on giving others a way to question the measurement and correct mistakes, including controlled review where public release is unsuitable. With the anatomy in place, we now build one agentic evaluation for a real use case: an agent that analyzes measurements for a physics lab. Rather than starting from scratch, we adapt an open task, so most of our effort goes into domain expertise and validation. sources.name: OpenAI
sources.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
sources.text: Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT‑6 Luna for their conversations. Beyond knowing how to answer a customer’s request, AI support agents need to be able to execute a solution. And for that, they need access to the right tools and instructions. According to Richpanel CEO Amit RG, human support agents can use 20 or 30 tools to serve a customer, and the procedures they follow may never have been written down. Richpanel ⁠ (opens in a new window) solves that using OpenAI models to both set up the tools and procedures AI support agents need to act and handle customer conversations. “The intelligence is no longer the bottleneck. It’s everything around it.” Deploying a support agent often requires a forward-deployed engineer to connect the agent to a customer’s systems and define how it should work. Amit saw that many companies didn’t have engineers to spare and asked himself, “What if that forward-deployed engineer itself was an AI agent?” So Richpanel built it: an AI manager to handle agent setup. Customers began calling it Boss AI. It writes procedures and defines how Richpanel’s frontline support agent, copilot, and quality-assurance agent call the tools they need. Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol for Boss AI, prioritizing accuracy when building the tools and procedures its other agents will follow. Richpanel designs the frontline agent to handle hundreds of thousands of conversations, making the cost of each interaction an important part of model selection. It uses GPT‑6 Luna and other OpenAI models for that work. Amit says Richpanel takes the same approach to its copilot and quality-assurance agents. “What matters is a balance of cost and intelligence,” Amit says. Richpanel’s customers may already use low-cost outsourced support. Automating their operations has to make financial sense against that starting point. Amit credits OpenAI with making models available that can handle long context and longer tasks while remaining cost efficient. Richpanel can use deeper reasoning to prepare its support agents and more economical models to run the conversations that follow. At the time of the October 2026 interview, Amit said Richpanel had completed approximately 300 AI customer-support deployments over the previous six months. The company guarantees customers a 50% automation rate within the first 30 days or their money back. Amit says it met that commitment across all of those deployments, adding, “In each of the cases, the AI is beating human support agents when it comes to customer satisfaction.” Product updates, practical guides, upcoming events, and more.

sources.name: NVIDIA
sources.title: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season
sources.text: The elves don’t have to be the only ones busy in the workshop this holiday season. With the lights twinkling and the gift wrap out, it’s the perfect time to give someone — or yourself — a spark to take a hobby to the next level. For some, that means diving into a new game. For others, it’s video editing or even building a robot. NVIDIA technologies offer something for everyone on Santa’s list. Read on to unwrap the details. With the holiday break here, everyone can be online to score bragging rights or explore a world that’s only been seen in video game trailers. For some players, an upgrade means a desktop that brings out the detail in every scene. For others, it’s a laptop they can take along when visiting family, or a way to play in the cloud on a device they already own. The right setup depends on where and what to play: For creators with a project that’s been on the backburner, the right gift this season can be the push to finally make it happen. Maybe it’s holiday clips becoming a short film, a snowy scene coming together in 3D or a livestream that brings friends across time zones to the same virtual table. Creators can use NVIDIA systems — such as GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX Spark devices — to keep up with the workflows, along with NVIDIA Studio tools and technologies for AI acceleration. Studio Drivers support video editing, 3D design and livestreaming. In supported applications, faster processing gives more room to experiment and refine. Every robot starts somewhere. This season, it could be under the tree. Building a robot is an experiment in teaching a device to see or sense its surroundings. A first project might be as simple as using a camera to identify a candy cane or a gingerbread man, then moving on to an app that probes what the camera sees. Testing brings new questions. Can the robot recognize the candy cane under twinkling lights? Can it tell a frosted gingerbread man from an unfrosted one? Each experiment leaves more to improve and explore. The NVIDIA Jetson edge AI platform provides the hardware and software to build projects like these. It combines compact computers with the NVIDIA JetPack software development kit to help makers build robots, autonomous machines and intelligent devices. A Jetson Developer Kit is a gift to explore computer vision, generative AI and multimodal robot control, with the option to add cameras and sensors suited to various projects. AI runs directly on the device, processing information from its surroundings. When ready to take a prototype further, production systems powered by Jetson modules provide a path to deployment. See how Microduck comes to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super , bringing together robot movement, visual understanding and natural-language interaction. With Hermes Agent and NVIDIA Cosmos, developers can explore how AI connects everyday requests with actions in the physical world. Bring an SO-101 arm to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin and explore agentic robotics. Give OpenClaw a simple request, and watch it plan the steps, call NVIDIA tools and check the results. OpenShell runs the agent securely in a sandbox, controlling its access to models and robot tools. Based on ASPIRE skills, the system reuses lessons from past attempts to guide future tasks. Build a robot companion that chats, moves and understands what it sees, with NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Cosmos open models running locally on Jetson Orin Nano 8GB. For more advanced projects, explore vision language action models and world action models to enable increasingly sophisticated robotic behaviors — beyond simple perception and predefined actions toward understanding natural language instructions, reasoning, planning multistep tasks and interacting with the physical world. Dive into setup guides and project tutorials in Jetson AI Lab . Whether it’s a gaming upgrade, a creative project or a first robot, the right tools can open up new possibilities well beyond the holidays. Explore NVIDIA’s holiday lineup for gamers, creators and makers.

sources.name: Google Research
sources.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
sources.text: Kyriakos Axiotis, Staff Research Scientist, and Thomas Fu, Principal Engineer, Google Research We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly. If a network has dozens or hundreds of layers, the original learning signal can become severely degraded or lost by the time it reaches all layers, which is known as the vanishing gradient problem in AI. To overcome this challenge and enable the training of networks with dozens or hundreds of layers, transformers rely heavily on residual connections , also known as “skip” connections, which act like an information highway or a shortcut. Instead of forcing the data to pass exclusively through the complicated layer, a duplicate copy of the original input skips right past this layer and is added directly to its output. This ensures that the model always has the original raw data to refer back to. The standard residual connection implements a simple operation: point-wise summation of a layer's output with its input. While computationally efficient, this simple process has a key limitation: it treats all prior representations with equal weight, leading to information dilution in deep networks. As features propagate through many layers, specific, high-resolution details from earlier layers can be averaged out or distorted, making it difficult for the network to selectively retrieve them. This forces the network to recompute them, reducing learning efficiency. In our ICML 2025 paper, "DeepCrossAttention: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections ," we studied the shortcomings of the traditional residual architecture and introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), which generalizes residual connections by allowing each layer to dynamically select and route features from the history of preceding layers. By allowing the model to dynamically choose which previous layers are most important at any given moment, DCA achieves comparable or improved learning, while reducing the number of parameters needed by up to 30-40%. Instead of treating skip connections as a rigid, additive pipeline, DCA reframes residual learning as a dynamic routing problem. Rather than passing all prior layers forward with equal weight, DCA introduces a lightweight, layer-wise module that decides how to best combine previous embeddings on a per-token basis. Comparison between a standard residual network and DeepCrossAttention (DCA). While a standard residual network uses rigid, additive point-wise connections with equal weighting, DCA introduces dynamic, learned routing weights (W) that allow each layer to selectively route and combine features from across the history of preceding layers. The architecture introduces two primary mechanisms: By allowing the network to dynamically select and retrieve high-resolution features from earlier layers, DCA eliminates the information dilution inherent to classic residual connections. To test whether DCA can overcome information dilution in practice, we evaluated our approach across controlled synthetic setups, large-scale language modeling benchmarks, and image classification tasks. DCA demonstrated significant improvements in convergence speed, training stability, and final model quality across these experiments. Perplexity (PPL) — how well a probability model predicts a sample — comparison across language modeling benchmarks. On both the LM1B (top) and C4 (bottom) datasets, DeepCrossAttention (DCA) achieves lower perplexity than standard transformers and alternative connection baselines (such as LAUREL-PA, 1x1-DenseFormer, and Hyper-Connections) under the same parameter and training budgets. On the colossal, cleaned version of Common Crawl's web crawl corpus (C4) and 1 Billion Word Language Model Benchmark ( LM1B ) datasets, DCA reached the performance of standard transformers in up to five times fewer training steps. When trained for the same duration or number of steps, DCA consistently achieved lower perplexity — how well a probability model predicts a sample — than standard residual connections, effectively extracting more representational capacity from the same training budget. To achieve a perplexity of <14 on LM1B, a standard transformer with fixed width required 42 layers, whereas the DCA model achieved a lower perplexity with only 30 layers — a 29% reduction in depth and parameter count. Impact of varying connection history (k) on model perplexity. Performance comparison showing how scaling the number of preceding layer connections in DCA consistently improves language modeling perplexity over the standard Transformer baseline, achieving the lowest perplexity at higher configurations (16-DCA and 24-DCA). One of the most common trade-offs in AI is that better models are often much larger and slower to run. DCA adds a tiny number of parameters — less than 0.2% of the total model size — making it negligible in terms of compute and memory footprint, while increasing memory bandwidth, as representations from different layers are presented intact rather than blended together. Interestingly, because DCA can be initialized to behave identically to a standard residual network, it doesn’t require training from scratch: retrofitting DCA onto an already pre-trained transformer and briefly continuing training reduced perplexity by 0.19 on LM1B, compared to just 0.02 for continued standard training. stories.title: Researchers Are Using Meta’s Open-Weight AI Models to Transform Medicine
stories.summary: We brought researchers together for the Open Source AI For Science Summit, where they shared how they’re using AI to accelerate scientific discovery. The post Researchers Are Using Meta’s Open-Weight AI Models to Transform Medicine appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.title: Researchers Are Using Meta’s Open-Weight AI Models to Transform Medicine
sources.text: Open science is critical to advancing medical research. To accelerate this progress, we’ve expanded our academic partnerships , giving researchers funding and access to our AI models like Muse Glimmer, SAM3, DINOv3, and Brain2Qwertyv2. These researchers are independently adapting our models for their own investigational research. Here are a few of the projects that are benefitting from our partnership: At Louisiana State University, Dr. Peter DeBlieux and his team are using Muse Glimmer, SAM 3, DINOv3, and other models from Meta, along with Meta Quest 3 headsets to develop COPES, an experimental coaching platform that supports healthcare professionals with medical procedural training in virtual reality. The system will aim to provide adaptive guidance, real-time performance assessment, and personalized feedback across technical execution, patient communication, clinical reasoning, and decision-making. Working virtually means medical students can learn complicated procedures in situations where practicing on real patients may be risky, and virtual instruction means more medical professionals can receive high quality technical and communications training — no matter where they are. Dr. Pierre Bourdillon at Rothschild Hospital Foundation is using AI research and models from Meta including NeuralSet , Brain2Qwertyv2 , Tribev2 , and DINOv3 , in research projects aimed at better understanding the source of epilepsy in the brain. Currently, epilepsy can’t be directly visualized in brain images, making it difficult for clinicians to identify its source. Dr. Bourdillon is using AI to develop a tool that can enable simulations of epileptic seizures originating in different regions of the brain. This approach could one day enable doctors to select the simulation that best matches their patient’s case, allowing them to form a strong hypothesis about where the patient’s epilepsy originates. This early-stage research could improve accuracy in a range of epilepsy treatments, including surgical removal of affected brain tissue and device implantation designed to disrupt epileptic activity. The simulations also have the potential to help researchers address speech and motor restoration in patients with brain injuries. At Columbia University, Dr. Wolfgang Pernice has partnered with Meta to adapt the DINO family of models to improve analysis of microscopy images of cells, helping doctors understand how rare diseases appear in cells. In conventional image analysis methods, researchers have to know what they are looking for in advance, limiting their analysis. But the adapted Cell-DINO, DINO-BoC, and FINO models generate unbiased representations of the inner workings of cells, allowing scientists to decode the complex patterns by which rare diseases manifest in human cells. This can help improve our understanding of rare diseases and accelerate drug discovery. Each of these investigational projects highlights AI’s unique ability to fill critical research gaps. While all of the work featured here is early-stage, we look forward to the potential breakthroughs enabled by our AI models. To learn more about our Open Source AI for Science Summit, where we interviewed the researchers, head to our AI blog .

recent_posts.summary: O Google reescreveu o aplicativo para rodar em aparelhos com pouca memória da linha Android Go, levando o assistente de IA a mais usuários.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia lança minidesktops RTX Spark para rodar IA local
recent_posts.summary: Computadores compactos da Asus, da Dell e da MSI usam a plataforma RTX Spark para rodar agentes, gerar imagem e vídeo e ajustar modelos sem depender da nuvem, segundo a Nvidia.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI usa seus modelos de IA para melhorar projeto de chips com a AMD
recent_posts.summary: A empresa diz ter reduzido área de circuitos do seu chip Jalapeño e, em parceria com a AMD, melhorado métricas de desempenho de GPUs e CPUs, segundo comunicado oficial.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic fecha IPO em US$ 119,5 bi com aporte de fabricantes de chip
recent_posts.summary: A empresa confirmou o exercício total da opção dos subscritores e uma colocação privada com AMD, Broadcom, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia e outras, segundo comunicado oficial.

recent_posts.title: Meta leva o Muse, seu agente pessoal de IA, para a Austrália
recent_posts.summary: Com parceiros locais em compras, imóveis e academia, o assistente chega ao terceiro mercado confirmado, segundo a própria empresa.

recent_posts.title: Ações da Anthropic caem no segundo dia e arrastam a Nasdaq
recent_posts.summary: A dona do Claude recuou perto do preço do IPO enquanto chips e bolsas da Ásia e da Europa também caíam, segundo o Guardian e a CNBC.

recent_posts.title: Matemático da Anthropic diz ter resolvido a Hipótese de Riemann
recent_posts.summary: Levent Alpöge publicou a demonstração em seu site pessoal dias após o IPO da Anthropic; a prova ainda não foi verificada de forma independente.

recent_posts.title: Apple contrata engenheiros para criar agente de IA próprio
recent_posts.summary: Vaga removida descrevia um assistente capaz de operar o computador inteiro, segundo a Bloomberg, citada pela TechCrunch e pelo The Verge.

recent_posts.title: Onda de apagões nos EUA reabre debate sobre o papel da IA
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft, FAA, bancos e Apple Pay falharam em dias recentes; autoridades negam ataque, mas especialistas discordam sobre o papel da IA.

recent_posts.title: Sete fundadores da Anthropic embolsam US$ 280 milhões cada no IPO
recent_posts.summary: Documentos da abertura de capital mostram que Amazon e Google também ficam com 28% da empresa, segundo TechCrunch e Fortune.

recent_posts.title: Trump ameaça taxar empresas dos EUA por data centers no exterior
recent_posts.summary: Em coletiva na Casa Branca, presidente disse que vai impedir empresas americanas de erguer data centers em outros países e prometeu um "imposto tremendo" para quem descumprir, segundo a CNBC e o The Verge.
